name: Electric Micromobility Device
description: From January 1, 2027, a light electric device for personal transportation operated at up to 28 mph: an electric skateboard, an electric unicycle, or a stand-up electric scooter, whether a low-speed one of 15 mph or less or a high-speed one past that, at any motor power. It counts as a motor vehicle but needs no title, registration, license or insurance; riders must be 16 and may use roads, bike lanes and bike paths but not sidewalks.

restrictions.rule: A light-weight, low-speed, electric-powered device used mainly for personal transportation and operated at speeds up to 28 mph; no limit on motor power or weight
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §1-117.6, added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Includes electric skateboards, self-balancing one-wheeled electric unicycles, and low-speed and high-speed electric scooters; excludes electric personal assistive mobility devices (self-balancing two-wheelers limited to 15 mph) and toy vehicles (battery ride-ons for children under 8, limited to 10 mph)
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §§1-117.6, 1-117.7, 1-117.8, 1-117.9, 1-205.5, as added and amended by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: A stand-up scooter has 2 or 3 wheels, handlebars and a floorboard, and is powered only by an electric motor and human power. It's a low-speed electric scooter when it weighs under 100 pounds and tops out at 15 mph or less, and a high-speed electric scooter when it can go faster than 15 mph; neither is a moped or motor driven cycle
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §§1-140.11, 1-125.11, as added and amended by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Counts as a motor vehicle, but needs no certificate of title, registration, driver's license or liability insurance
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §§1-117.6, 3-102, 3-402, 6-102, 7-601, as amended by SB 3484 (2026)
Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(d), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: May carry a passenger only if it was designed to carry more than one person, and a rider may not attach it or themself to another vehicle on a roadway
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(g), (h), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: May not be ridden under the influence of alcohol or any drug
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(j), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: May be ridden on any highway, street, roadway, bicycle lane or bicycle path without impeding traffic, with a vehicle driver's rights and duties
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(a), (n), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: May not be ridden on a sidewalk, on an interstate, or on a highway with a speed limit above 35 mph unless it has a bicycle lane
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(b), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: One capable of going faster than 28 mph and ridden that fast is barred from every public highway, whatever its speed limit, and from bicycle lanes and bicycle paths
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(b), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: May be parked wherever a bicycle may, without blocking a sidewalk or pedestrian right-of-way
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(f), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Must have a working brake and be kept in good operating condition; at night it needs a white front lamp visible at 500 feet and a red rear reflector or a red lamp visible at 500 feet; no siren, except on a police or fire department device
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(e), (k), (l), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: No one may knowingly tamper with or modify its speed capability or motor engagement beyond its original speed capability
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(i), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Police may confiscate and impound one ridden or found in violation of these rules, and release it for an administrative fee, waived when it was stolen
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(m), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Breaking these rules is a petty offense for a first or second conviction, and a Class C misdemeanor for a third within a year

The Department of Transportation and the Department of Natural Resources may ban it from highways, bicycle lanes and paths they control, and park, forest preserve, conservation and transit districts may regulate it on their bicycle paths; no other unit of local government, home-rule units included, may regulate it
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1435(c), (o), added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Can't be made, sold, leased, rented or used in a business unless an accredited lab has certified its electrical system to UL 2272, and a replacement battery to UL 2271; batteries rebuilt from used cells can't be sold, and a violation is consumer fraud
restrictions.citation: Micromobility Fire Safety Act, 815 ILCS 361/10, 361/15, 361/20, 361/25 (P.A. 104-414), as amended by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Before 2027 only a stand-up electric scooter of 10 mph or less had a class of its own, the low-speed electric scooter: riders had to be 18, and it was allowed only where a municipality, a park, forest preserve or conservation district, or the Department of Natural Resources authorized it, never on state highways or highways posted above 35 mph
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §§1-140.11, 11-1518, repealed by SB 3484 (2026)
